topic: Neural Networks: The Blueprint of Artificial Intelligence

sections.title: The Biological Inspiration: The Puppy Analogy
lecture_lines: Neural networks learn from experience, much like a puppy.
Meet Pixel, a digital puppy learning to recognize objects.
Pixel uses color and shape to distinguish balls from lemons.
animations: Fade in digital puppy 'Pixel' and two objects: yellow lemon and red ball.
Display text 'Input: Yellow + Round' near the lemon object.
Animate 'Pixel' looking at lemon with a '?' appearing above.
Label lemon as 'Snack' (#00FF00) and ball as 'Toy' (#0000FF).
Show 'Pixel' puppy smiling after correctly identifying the red ball.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Linear Equation as a Slider
lecture_lines: Every neuron uses the basic formula: y equals wx plus b.
The weight, w, determines the signal's strength or sensitivity.
The bias, b, sets the threshold for making a decision.
animations: Display formula y = wx + b in white (#FFFFFF) at top.
Animate slider for 'w' (weight) making the line steeper on axes.
Animate slider for 'b' (bias) shifting the line up and down.

sections.title: The Artificial Neuron: The Mathematical Heart
lecture_lines: A neuron gathers inputs and calculates a weighted sum.
Think of this sum as a funnel collecting information.
The result then passes through an activation function gatekeeper.
Activation functions, like ReLU, determine if the neuron fires.
The neuron output depends on if math exceeds the threshold.
animations: Draw a neuron circle (#FFD700) with incoming arrows for inputs.
Show inputs labeled as x_1, x_2 with weights w_1, w_2.
Display summation formula sum(w_i * x_i) + b inside the neuron.
Transform summation into a blue (#0000FF) Sigmoid S-curve graph.
Animate output arrow y glowing as the input sum increases.

sections.title: Layered Architecture: The Assembly Line
lecture_lines: Neurons organize into input, hidden, and output layers.
Data flows forward, becoming more abstract at each stage.
Raw pixels transform into complex patterns like digit shapes.
animations: Show a digit '7' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/seven.svg] image on left, split into pixel [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pixel.svg] grid.
Display Input, Hidden, and Output layers with connecting lines.
Animate light pulse flowing through layers to the '7' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/seven.svg] output.

sections.title: The Math of Connectivity: Matrix Multiplication
lecture_lines: Layers communicate through massive grids of connections called matrices.
We use matrix multiplication to calculate many neurons at once.
The dot product sums up all weighted inputs simultaneously.
Brightly glowing connections represent high-strength weights in the grid.
This parallel processing makes modern AI fast and efficient.
animations: Display Vector X (Input) and Matrix W (Weights) in white (#FFFFFF).
Animate dot product: row of W meeting column of X with flash.
Show a grid of connections between layers glowing by weight strength.
Display equation Y = WX + B in gold (#FFD700).
Animate all output neurons lighting up simultaneously for parallel calc.

sections.title: Learning via Feedback: The Error Correction
lecture_lines: After a guess, the network compares it to the truth.
A loss function calculates the distance between guess and reality.
Backpropagation identifies which weights caused the specific error.
The network wiggles weights to minimize the calculated loss.
Through repeated feedback, Pixel correctly identifies the lemon.

Animate network connections vibrating/wiggling to indicate weight adjustment.
Visually change connection thickness and show error value decreasing.
